text:
An electrical engineer has made a pair of components P and Q.
The resistance of P decreases as the temperature rises. The resistance of Q increases as the
temperature rises.
The total resistance of P and Q in series remains constant when the temperature changes. The
two components are connected in series with a power source supplying a constant current.
Which statement is correct?
A
If a temperature change causes the potential difference (p.d.) across P to double, the p.d.
across Q will always halve.
B
The difference between the p.d. across P and the p.d. across Q does not change with
temperature.
C
The p.d. across component P increases as the temperature rises.
D
The sum of the p.d. across P and the p.d. across Q does not change with temperature.
